A long time ago, in a much earlier stage of my life, I took time to go hike around the northern parts of South America. I figured I was fluent in Spanish, so I should be fine. I ran into a few like-minded people and we determined we'd make our next destination Brazil. It was much cheaper to fly and customs wasn't nearly as nosey about what was in our luggage, so we packed our nose candy, clothing, and meandered off to Brazil.

Once in the country, we soon learned that Spanish wasn't actually the primary language spoken and the area we'd landed in wasn't actually full of Spanish speakers. So, we did mounds of cocaine and enjoyed the beaches where skimpy clothing was pretty much the most clothing you'd see anyone wearing.

Hmm... I was still in what you'd probably call high school, so I think that might have been the summer of 1974. No, I don't remember it just like it was yesterday. We did all manage to get laid, and a subset of the population did speak Spanish. It was a grand adventure and they certainly didn't care about our ages when we wanted to order alcohol.

It was remarkably inexpensive. The whole summer, including flights, was less than $1,000. I remember because I'd saved like $1,200 bucks and still had like $600 left when I got back and my dear mum had only wired me maybe $100 during the whole summer. Good times, really. I'd suggest that all young people would be better off if they got the chance to travel and see the world.
